newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: S.Lanka rupee ends low on commercial dlr demand.
newsitem.headline: S.Lanka rupee ends low on commercial dlr demand.

text.p: The Sri Lanka rupee, which came off the day's low against the dollar, closed down on import covering demand for the greenback, dealers said.
The rupee closed at 58.80 to the dollar after opening at 58.75 and falling to a low of 58.86, they said.
"Whenever commercial demand for dollars pushed down the rupee to 58.86, there was firm resistance," said an American Express Bank dealer.
Speculators were marginally active, banking on continuing commercial demand for the U.S. unit and its maintaining its strength overseas, dealers said.
Low overnight call money rates also helped speculation, said one.
Overnight call money was at 8.75 percent, with the Central Bank overnight repo rate at 8.5, dealers said.
Dealer say cheap call money and overall demand for the U.S. unit could take the exchange rate to 59 rupees to the dollar, in the coming week.
